problem: Existing navigation instruction generators (speaker models) produce a single style from one dataset, have limited linguistic quality, offer no control over style or landmark content, and mostly ignore the spatial topology of the environment.
motivation: Instruction generation is needed for human-robot collaboration, guidance for the visually impaired, and building human-machine trust. Useful instructions must be executable and controllable: abstraction level should match how familiar the recipient is with the place, and landmarks should be adjustable. LLMs offer strong language ability, but they lack embodied spatial knowledge and annotated data are limited.
key_idea: Adapt a LLaMA-Adapter LLM with a trajectory encoder, and use chain-of-thought landmark prompting (CoTL), a spatial topology auxiliary task (STMT) and mixed-style prompt training (SMT) to generate style- and content-controllable instructions.
insight: Predicting landmarks first and then conditioning the instruction on them gives content controllability, since edited landmarks change the instruction. It also raises SPICE on REVERIE val-unseen from 0.129 to 0.141. STMT (predicting the backtracking action) gives the largest gain on abstract instructions (REVERIE unseen CIDEr 0.397 to 0.490) and curbs overfitting. Mixing styles also improves quality, and an incremental ablation shows every component helps. Instructions from C-Instructor are close to human ones when followed by navigators, whereas prior speakers' instructions hurt data augmentation.
method: Trajectory Encoder: CLIP ViT-L/14 features for the 36 subviews of each panorama, plus view-position, history and action/non-action tokens, aggregated by 8 ViT blocks with M aggregator tokens per step.
LLM Adapter: LLaMA-Adapter (7B) with layer-wise adapters and zero-initialized attention that inject trajectory tokens into the LLM; only the last 2 LLM layers are finetuned.

STMT: auxiliary task predicting the action that returns to the previous viewpoint. It uses a special token, cross-attention over the 36 views from layer L_s=30, and an attention-based classification head with cross-entropy loss trained jointly.

CoTL: two-stage generation. The first stage predicts landmarks (nouns from instructions plus visual landmarks selected by temporal feature-change and spatial distinctiveness scores, threshold beta=0.25). The second stage generates the instruction conditioned on those landmarks, which the user can edit.
SMT: jointly train on R2R, REVERIE, RxR (and UrbanWalk) with different prompts per style, so one model can switch style by prompt.
Training: pretrain on PREVALENT for 240K iterations, then fine-tune jointly on multiple datasets for 120K iterations.

setting.backbone: LLaMA-Adapter multimodal LLM (LLaMA 7B, last 2 layers fine-tuned) + CLIP ViT-L/14 (frozen) + 8-block ViT trajectory encoder
setting.training_data: PREVALENT pretraining (240K iters), then joint fine-tuning on R2R, REVERIE, RxR (English) and UrbanWalk (120K iters)
setting.observation: Panoramic RGB (36 subviews per viewpoint) along a given path with action index
setting.action_space: Not applicable (text generation); STMT selects a candidate view for backtracking in a discrete nav graph
setting.privileged: Ground-truth paths given as input (instruction generation task); landmarks from GT instructions used in training only

numbers.extra: Instruction generation (text metrics); PREVALENT pretraining and multi-dataset SMT

numbers_note: Main metrics are text-similarity scores for instruction generation, not navigation success. User study: 15 students, 100 REVERIE val-unseen paths, mean score 3.50 vs Lana 2.26.
results: C-Instructor beats BT-, EDrop-, CCC-speaker and LANA on all four benchmarks (R2R, REVERIE, RxR, UrbanWalk). For example, on R2R val-unseen SPICE is 0.212 vs 0.174 for Lana (best baseline). Instructions guide navigators nearly as well as human ones (HAMT SR 31.35 vs 32.95). As data augmentation, C-Instructor raises HAMT SR from 32.95 to 34.25, while the other speakers lower it. Human study score is 3.50 vs 2.26 for the best baseline.
limitations: Trained only on simulated discrete-viewpoint data, so real-world continuous environments are not handled.
Weak modeling of global environment structure (e.g., confuses floor levels) and misidentifies rare objects.
Text metrics are weakly correlated with semantic quality; SMT gains are small and sometimes mixed across metrics.
